newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call rate slips on Central Bank rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila call rate slips on Central Bank rate cut.

text.p: The Philippine call loan rate slipped to 13.03125 percent on Friday in step with the one percentage point cut in the Central Bank's benchmark overnight rate to 13 percent earlier in the day, traders said.
The average interbank rate had been stuck at 14.03125 percent in recent days.
"The market just followed the Central Bank's lead," one trader said.
Volume was moderate at 12.328 billion pesos as some banks had to cover their reserve deficiencies for two days. Thursday was a holiday as the nation marked its 99th Independence Day.
On the other hand, short-term secondary Treasury bill rates rose as traders tried to lock in their investments in longer-termed instruments before rates fell further.
"Some banks were gapping. They lightened up their short-term bills and loaded longer-termed bills," another trader said.
Other banks were expecting rates to go up at Monday's auction, believing the rates had bottomed already.
A survey of eight banks showed firmer bid-offer quotes across all maturities.
